key_insight: Publicly available policies at U.S. osteopathic medical schools usually mention relevant patient-information issues, but rarely give clear scenario-specific decision support.
clinical_relevance: For students and clinicians, this means policy lookup may not be enough; many situations still require local interpretation, supervision, or escalation.
method: Exploratory vignette-based document analysis across 20 U.S. osteopathic medical schools
Eight patient-information vignettes produced 160 school-vignette pairs
Three AI-assisted retrieval-and-evaluation runs per pair, with investigator verification of discordant cases
evidence_signal: Of 160 school-vignette pairs, 159 had at least one eligible source, but only 21 (13.1%) were judged to provide sufficient support after combining explicit and inferable guidance.
watch_item: This was a nonprobability sample of schools and an AI-assisted document review, so results may not generalize and may depend on how policies are written and interpreted.
paper_title: Decision Support in Publicly Available Patient Information Policies at U.S. Osteopathic Medical Schools: A Vignette-Based Document Analysis
